route: /style-board/ (the style board: module process:photo-cards, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: The line that opens the section, 'How size-by-size print placement works', is the block's lead with no heading above it, so it renders at body size and regular weight. That makes it smaller and lighter than the bold card titles under it, and the section reads upside down. m7-steps' 'Care steps from our rash guard labels.' has the same problem at both widths. The earlier review sent this to content, but reference.css already has a rule for leads without a heading (lines 366–367); it covers the list and timeline variants and leaves out photo-cards.
findings.reference: The competitor opens its sections with a bold heading above the cards, heavier than the card titles.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process:not(:has(> .process__heading)) > .block__lead` to the selector at lines 366–367. That sets the lead in the heading face at --size-card-heading, at the heading weight, in --heading-color (white here).

findings.issue: The earlier review asked for wider side padding, and it is still not applied. Each card keeps about 20px on each side (card 01: outline at x 434, text at x 455), against about 40px above the title under the number badge, so titles and text sit close to the white outline. The desktop cards show the same, in both blocks.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards pad their content evenly on every side, about 32px.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `padding-inline: 2rem` on `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step` (patterns.css:605 still sets 1.25rem). Move the `.process-step__marker` left offset to the same 2rem so the badge stays over the title's edge.

findings.issue: Each stacked card still has about 50px of empty space under its last line, against about 40px above the title, so every card looks bottom-heavy. For example, card 01 ends its text near y 640 and its outline near y 690. This was reported before and the shots show it unchanged; m3-steps' cards show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards use the same padding on every side, so the content sits evenly inside the outline.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `margin-bottom: 0` on `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step > :last-child`, so the card's own bottom padding (1.5rem) is the only space under the text.
